newsitem.title: UK: Brent trades steady, most N.Sea grades quiet.
newsitem.headline: Brent trades steady, most N.Sea grades quiet.

text.p: One of the last July-loading Brent cargoes changed hands at a steady price on Tuesday but most North Sea grades marked time as traders digested fresh data on August loading programmes.
The cargo, loading July 24-26, was sold by a European major at a 12 cent discount to August Brent, traders said.
The buyer sold the cargo on to another major at the same differential.
The trades follow agreement on Monday on August -20 cents for a July 19-21 loader and August -10 cents agreed for a July 27-29 loader.
Other grades were inactive, with almost all July cargoes heading for homes. One exception is a European major that is believed to have two July-loading Forties and one Statfjord.
Traders with requirements for those grades said they want to see the values achieved on those cargoes before committing to August barrels.

"Overall it's been pretty dull," said a trader. "People are hanging back, waiting for all the pgorammes to come out and see a day of consolidation in values before making any more activity on the physical side."
The Brent trades helped supportthe paper market, where CFDs gained three to five cents in sympathy after languishing for much of the day around Monday's numbers.
CFDs for next week were talked five cents firmer at September Brent -20/-15 cents, with the following week two to three cents up at September -25/-21 cents.
The outright price won support from a buoyant U.S. gasoline market. August IPE Brent was 26 cents firmer at $18.08 a barrel at 1735 GMT.
NYMEX gasoline surged on talk that this week's API report will show possibly the last big drawdown of unleaded stocks of the summer.
Brent also drew early strength from August loading programmes showing volumes slightly below expectations.
Brent system operator Shell Expro estimated North Sea Brent crude system throughput in August at 407,800 barrels per day (bpd), slightly lower than the 409,076 bpd pumped in July.
The loading programmes for Ekofisk and Flotta are expected to be issued on Wednesday.

The issue of Iraq's oil exports, and particularly the timetable of the renewed sales, continues to hang over the market. Traders say business will continue to be slow as long as further details about timing remain scarce.
